newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Arafat says no meeting yet set with Netanyahu.
newsitem.headline: Arafat says no meeting yet set with Netanyahu.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat said on Wednesday no summit meeting between Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and himself had yet been arranged but reiterated he is "not against" it.
"I'm not against any meeting with Mr Netanyahu. But not only for propaganda," Arafat told a news conference in Vienna after meeting Austrian Foreign Minister Wolfgang Schuessel.

"I'm looking to have a constructive meeting to implement accurately and honestly what had been signed and what had been agreed upon in the White House under the supervision of President Clinton," he added.
Israeli-Palestinian talks have reached a stalemate over the long-delayed Israeli troop pullback in the West Bank town of Hebron due to security arrangements for Hebron's 400 Jews.
Israel is supposed to hand over 80 percent of Hebron to Palestinian rule, according to the 1995 agreement signed in Washington by Arafat and then-Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin.

Arafat, on the last day of his two-day official visit to Austria, called on Austria to capitalise on its role in the European Union and the international arena to help push forward the implementation, and protection, of the peace process.
"Especially after we're facing many challenges....we are in need of this push and for this support to protect the peace process -- and I'm sure we'll get it," he said.
